text: This chapter covered logical backups, physical backups, and point-in-time recovery as separate tools. A real disaster recovery plan puts them together, sized against actual business requirements — the same RPO and RTO discipline from every earlier platform in this path.

Your recovery point objective is set by how frequently WAL segments reach archive storage, not by your last base backup. Your recovery time objective is shaped by how long that base backup takes to restore plus how much WAL there is left to replay.

A complete plan documents backup cadence with verified archiving, retention for backups and WAL, a current globals dump for roles and tablespaces, and a restore procedure that's actually been rehearsed and timed.

An untested backup isn't a real backup here either — only the commands are PostgreSQL-specific, not the discipline. Next up, Chapter Fifteen: PostgreSQL performance tuning methodology, starting with measuring before you change anything.
